content.text:
Steven Pelayo
Managing Director, The Blueshirt Group
Thank you, Desmond. Good day, everyone. Thank you for joining us to discuss Q2 2024 results, which we released before the U.S .market opened today. The release is available on our website as well as from Newswire Services. There is also a supplemental slide deck posted to the investor section of our website that we will reference during our prepared remarks. On the call with me today are our CEO, David Wang, our CFO, Mark McKechnie, and Lisa Feng, our CFO of our operating subsidiary, ACM Shanghai. Before we continue, please turn to slide two.
Let me remind you that remarks made during this call may include predictions, estimates, or other information that might be considered forward-looking. These forward-looking statements represent ACM's current judgment for the future. However, they are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.
Those risks are described under the risk factors and elsewhere in ACM's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Please do not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which reflect ACM's opinions only as of the date of this call. ACM is not obliged to update you on any revisions to these forward-looking statements. Certain of these financial results we provide on this call will be on a non-GAAP basis, which excludes stock-based compensation and an unrealized gain or loss on short-term investments. For our GAAP results and a reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP amounts, you should refer to our slides.
Or pardon me, you should refer to our earnings release, which is posted on the IR section of our website and to slide 12. Let me now turn the call over to David Wang, who will begin with slide 3. David?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thanks, Steven. Hello, everyone, and welcome to ACM Research Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Please turn to slide 3. For the second quarter, revenue was $202.5 million, up 40%. Shipments were $203 million, up 32%. Profitability was good, with a gross margin of 48.2% and operating margin of 25.6%. We ended the quarter with approximately $367 million of cash and time deposit, with a positive cash flow from operation for the quarter. Revenue for the H1 of the year was $354.7 million dollars, up 62%. We believe this growth rate is higher than the growth rate of China WFE and demonstrates market share gain for ACM and the contribution from new product cycles.
Now I will provide detail on product. Please turn to slide 4. Revenue from single wafer cleaning, Tahoe, and semi-critical cleaning product grew 36% in Q2, and represented 76% of total revenue. ACM offer what we believe is among the industry most comprehensive cleaning portfolio. We estimate the global total addressable market, or TAM, for cleaning is close to $6 billion, and ACM produce products supporting 90% of all cleaning process steps in both the memory and the logic. During the last earnings call, we highlight the sulfuric peroxide, or SPM, portion of the cleaning market, which has been a relatively small contributor to our business, but represented 25% to 30% of the total front-end cleaning market. ACM now offer a full product line of SPM tool across all temperature range.
We have already shipped Tahoe and the single wafer tools for lower and middle temperature SPM steps. We now have a differentiated high temperature SPM tool that we believe position us to gain market share from the current market leader. We currently have more than 10 SPM customer in production or evaluation, and look forward to increase contribution to shipment or revenue as we ramp in production in the next 12 to 24 months. We also expect our Bevel Etch cleaning tool to contribute in more revenue in 2024, and we are on track to complete evaluation of a supercritical CO2 dry cleaning tool this year, and the revenue in 2025. We believe ACM cleaning portfolio, including SAPS, TEBO, Tahoe, semi-critical, together with SPM and supercritical CO2 dry, has achieved world-class status.
We see good opportunity for continued market share gain in mainland China. We are confident we have what it takes to secure major customer in the international markets. Revenue from ECP, furnace, and other technology grow 104% in Q2 and represent 19% of total revenue. We achieved another quarterly record in this category with nearly $39 million in revenue in Q2. In plating, we are seeing strong demand for both front-end wafer processing and back-end packaging. We have a major new product announcement today, the Ultra ECP ap plating tool for the next generation fan-out panel-level packaging or FOPLP. We believe this is a game-changing that position ACM to participate in growing demand for AI solutions. Our proprietary design employ a horizontal plating method that deliver film uniformity and the precision across the entire panel.
We believe ACM is among the first to employ horizontal plating for panel application, and it will strengthen the market, enabling advanced packaging with sub-micron feature on large panel. This technology especially applicable to GPU and a high density, high bandwidth memory HBM. We see a large opportunity as several major semiconductor leader have chosen panel for their AI chip packaging solution.
We continue to make good progress with our furnace product, which address more process step, ranging from oxidation, anneal to LPCVD and ALD. As noted in prior call, our furnace product cycle is about 18 months behind the plating. We believe our furnace product portfolio will benefit from increasing capacity for both memory and logic. Overall, we expect to have more than 60 furnace customer by end of this year compared to the 9 at end of our 2023.
Revenue from advanced packaging, which exclude ECP, but including service and spare, declined by 20% for Q2, but was up 13.5% for the H1 of the year. This category includes a range of packaging tools such as coater, developer, scrubber, pure stripper, and wet etchers, and also service and spare parts. We are exploring new product and technology to participate in the next generation of advanced packaging. We believe ACM is one of the only company that offers full set of wet tool, polish tool, and copper plating tool for advanced packaging. Last week, we announced the Ultra C v flux cleaning tool for fan-out panel level packaging. This is a companion tool to the ECP ap-p, which I mentioned earlier, and extending ACM product portfolio to the panel space.
In July, we shipped our first Ultra C v flux tool to a new Chinese packaging manufacturer. Put together, we believe those two panel tools, including plating and cleaning, mark a strong offering by ACM to address a fan-out panel-level packaging market. We believe ACM is among the first to applying horizontal plating technology into panel packaging application. We believe our technology will help accelerate ACM's global market share gain, as interest in panel-level packaging is growing rapidly among the foundry, IDM, and the OSAT in the U.S., Korea, and Taiwan, and Mainland China. Finish up on product. We are making good progress with our traction on PECVD platform. We believe our proprietary approach positioning both tools for success for mainland China and the global customer. We shipped our beta version of PECVD tool in July to a logic customer.
The innovative platform is capable of handling a wide variety of the PECVD process. We expect multiple evaluations this year and a number of our local customers in foundry, logic, memory, and other areas. We are moving forward in the development of our track tool, which has a differentiated design with a focus on high throughput and low maintenance. In addition to ALD evaluation tool in a major Chinese foundry, we are also engaging with several customers for i-line and KrF line based lithography. We expect good progress for both PECVD and track over the next year, with revenue likely in later 2025 and more notable contribution in 2026 and beyond. Moving on to customers. Please turn to slide 7. In Q2, we saw broader demand from foundry, logic, power, and memory, both NAND and DRAM.
For Q2 2024, we had four 10% customers representing 58% of the revenue versus three customers representing 52% in Q2 2023. In China, we have a leading position in cleaning with significant room to grow. We believe we have become a world-class multi-product company with competitive product in market for plating and furnace. We have a solid evaluation pipeline for track and PECVD. Overall, we believe our China growth is being driven by the market share gain, new product, and increased localization. In the U.S., we delivered the Ultra C b backside cleaning and the Bevel Etch tool in Q2 2024 to a large U.S. manufacturer that qualified as the first step cleaning tool for revenue later last year.
This demonstrates a deepened relationship which we believe can lead to a production order across multiple product lines. Today, I'm pleased to announce we have received an order from U.S..-based wafer-level packaging house for coater developer tool. We expect to deliver this tool to the U.S. facility in the H1 of 2025. Last month, we had a great week at the SEMICON West trade show in San Francisco. We had several days of solid meetings with a number of U.S. Chip makers with fabs in the U.S. and abroad. With good interest in our suite, TEBO, Tahoe, supercritical CO2 drying, plating, and our wet etch tools. In Europe, we are in the final stage of qualification of Ultra C VF cleaning tool at a major global semiconductor manufacturer.
In Korea, we engage with multiple customers for both front-end and packaging tool, including single wafer and batch clean, Tahoe, ECP, Furnace, ALD, PECVD, and Track. We see opportunity for our tool with SK hynix high bandwidth memory capacity product. To support growth, we made progress on our facility expansion in China and other regions. Please turn to slide 8. In China, our Lingang production and R&D center is nearly complete. We expect initial production to begin in the H2 of this year. In Korea, we believe a strong commitment can improve our relation with key Korean customers. Our resources in Korea can also provide another basis to support international customers. We continue investing in our Oregon site to add our service, support, and demonstration capability for R&D and customer activity in the U.S. and Europe.
In Q3, we entered into an agreement to purchase a 40,000 sq ft R&D facility in Oregon with a fully functional 5,000 sq ft clean room. The purchase is scheduled to close in Q4. This new facility demonstrates a strong commitment to the U.S. market, allows us to conduct R&D and demonstration of ACM technology near major semiconductor producers. Several years ago, we set a long-term revenue target of $1 billion. We are now close to this level, and we have made good progress with new product and international marketing. As a result, I'm happy to report that today we have set a new long-term revenue target of $3 billion. Please turn to slide 6. Key reasons for the increase include, first, we have scaled our business in Mainland China and also Korea.
We now ship cleaning, plating, and advanced packaging tool to nearly all the major and the smaller semiconductor manufacturers. We are amongst the top one or two local producer for each category. Second, we believe our product are world-class. This including our current offering and our new product roadmap. We are committed to innovation, and we believe we can compete head-to-head with the top-tier player, both in China and international market. At a high level, we believe a market share shift to AI is moving the market towards ACM technology, whereas.
We have been investing in key technology for years, and we are now seeing good interest to apply key technology to several industrial trends. Let me highlight a few. The shift to 3D structure for NAND, DRAM, and logic is driving demand for our vertical cleaning solution, including TEBO and supercritical CO2 dry.
Also our proprietary furnace ALD design. Next, HBM requires a driving demand for our TSV plating and 2.5D advanced packaging solutions. For PECVD, ACM has a very unique approach, including 1 chamber with 3 tracks that allow our customers to address multiple processes with the same platform. For track, ACM differentiated platform is designed for high throughput and no maintenance tool scanner. Therefore, panel plating, as we announced today, we believe ACM's new Ultra ECP ap-p is a game changer that will support future AI chip packaging at the panel level. Third, with our product line improving at scale in China and Korea, we are seeing good traction with our global customers. We have multiple tools under evaluation at several major customers in U.S., Europe, Korea, and Southeast Asia. We are confident those can lead to volume production orders.
In the longer term, we expect up to half our business in market beyond Mainland China. Bring it all together, our $3 billion target, assuming that China will account for about $1.5 billion revenue, and the rest of the world, which is 2 to 3x larger than China, will account for other $1.5 billion. I will now provide our outlook. Please turn to slide nine. We have raised our 2024 revenue outlook to be in a range of $695 to 735 million, versus prior outlook of $650 million to $725 million. At the middle point, our new outlook represent 28% year-over-year growth compared to 23% previously. We expect the shipment in the H2 of the year to grow, with the full year shipment growth rate outpacing revenue growth rate.
We note our visibility for the year is largely driven by our current order book. We anticipate the new orders and the qualification or customer acceptance of their previous shipped evaluation tool to a range of the customers. We believe WFE spending in mainland China will remain stable as the country continues to work on its goal to match the production capacity with end market consumption. We are focused on gaining market share in mainland China, launching our new products, and expanding our business to new customers in the US, Korea, Taiwan, Europe, and other South and Southeast Asia markets. Now let me turn the call over to our CFO, Mark, who will reveal details of our Q2 results. Mark, please.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thank you, David. Good day, everyone. Please turn to slide 10. Unless I note otherwise, I'll refer to non-GAAP financial measures, which exclude stock-based compensation, unrealized gain/loss on short-term investments. Reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to comparable GAAP measures is included in the earnings release. Unless otherwise noted, the following figures refer to Q2 2024, and comparisons are with Q2 2023. I will now provide financial highlights for Q2 2024. Revenue was $202.5 million, up 40%. Revenue for single wafer cleaning, Tahoe, and semi-critical cleaning was $153.2 million, up 36.2%. Revenue for ECP, front-end packaging, furnace, and other technologies was $39.0 million, up 103.8%.
Revenue for advanced packaging, excluding ECP, services and spares was $10.3 million for Q2, down 20.4%. For the H1, it grew by 13.5%. Total shipments were $203 million, up 32%. Gross margin was 48.2% versus 47.6%. This exceeded our long-term gross margin target of 40% to 45%. For the full year, we now expect our gross margins to be above the high end of the range. This is due to gross margins above the range for the H1 and our expectations for gross margin at the upper end of our target range for Q3 and Q4. We continue to expect gross margin to vary from period to period due to a variety of factors such as sales volume, product mix, and currency impacts.
Operating expenses were $45.6 million, up from $36.3 million. R&D was $21.8 million versus $19.4 million. The year-over-year increase primarily reflects additional personnel expenses to support our product development pipeline. Sales and marketing was $14.1 million versus $11 million, and G&A was $9.8 million versus $6.0 million. For 2024, we plan for R&D in the 13% to 15% range, sales and marketing in the 7% to 8% range, and G&A in the 5% to 6% range. Operating income was $51.9 million versus $32.4 million. Operating margin was 25.6% versus 22.4%. We had no realized gain from the sale of short-term investments for the quarter as compared to a gain of $3.9 million in the year ago period.
Recall that the realized gains are included in our non-GAAP earnings. Income tax expense was $9.3 million versus $7.6 million. For the full year, we plan for an effective tax rate on non-GAAP pre-tax income in the 15% to 20% range. Net income attributable to ACM Research was $37.3 million versus $31.3 million. Net income per diluted share was $0.55 versus $0.48. Our non-GAAP net income excluded $14.3 million or 21%, $0.21 per share in stock-based compensation expense. We note that due to the accelerated amortization for ACM Shanghai stock option grants, we do expect SBC expense to gradually roll off in the Q3 and beyond. I will now review selected balance sheet and cash flow items.
Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and time deposits ended Q2 at $366.8 million versus $288.3 million at the end of last quarter. Total inventory was $602.9 million versus $581.1 million at the end of last quarter. This included raw materials and work in process of $324.0 million and finished goods inventory of $278.9 million. Finished goods inventory mainly includes first tools under evaluation at our customers, also includes finished goods at ACM facilities. Cash flow from operations was $61 million for Q2 and $51.9 million for the H1 of the year. Capital expenses were $13.6 million for Q2, $39.7 million for the H1 of the year.
For the full year 2024, we expect to spend about $100 million in capital expenditures. This primarily includes continued investments in our Lingang facilities, remodeling for the new headquarters for ACM Shanghai, and our investments in Korea and the U.S., together with fixed asset expenditures. That concludes our prepared remarks. Now let us open the call for any questions that you may have. Operator, please go ahead.
Operator
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask questions on the phone, please press star one one and wait for your name to be announced. If you'd like to cancel your request, please press star one one again. One moment for the first question. Our first question comes from the line of Suji De Silva from Roth Capital. Please go ahead.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi, David, Mark, Lisa. Congrats on the progress here and the up guidance. For the H2, your shipments appear to be increasing. Can you talk about maybe 1% or give us some sense of how much of that shipment base is outside of China versus China, and how that'll increase in the mix over time?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Sure. Dave, do you wanna take that?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
You wanna take care, Mark?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah, sure. Hey, Suji. Thanks. Yeah. You did point out, yeah, that we expect our shipments to be a bit higher in the H2 versus the H1 of the year. You know, we'd expect shipments up obviously in Q3. In terms of the mix internationally or outside of Mainland China, Suji, I would say that the substantial majority of our shipments will still be within China. We will have some shipments outside, but really, substantial majority is gonna be to the Mainland China market in the back half of the year.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Yeah, thanks, Mark. Specifically for the Korea customers, I know you've been shipping into the China fabs for Korea customers, but are you already shipping into Korea fab for Korean customers? If not, what's the timing of that starting? 'Cause that sounds like something, newer as an opportunity I've heard versus kind of U.S. and Europe.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. We are definitely working with the Korean customer. At this moment, I mean, Q2, we have no shipment go there, Korea right now. However we do see the opportunity including also R&D tool and for their beyond the cleaning product. We're heavily engaged with the our Korean customer. We see that additional new product will hopefully can be shipping there H2, which is really another bigger high quarter product for the HBM production, right? That's where we're looking for.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Mm-hmm. Outstanding. That's great. My last question's on the high bandwidth memory supply chain in Taiwan, which has been growing very strong. Can you talk about your opportunity there, if that's soon and, who the competition today is in that market? Because we know with AI that's growing very fast.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. You mean the panel side, the new product? Suji, you mean that? Is that correct?
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
The high bandwidth memory opportunity, the supply chain then in the products, into that in China, in Taiwan rather.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. You mean our new panel product? You talk about our package-
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Yes. Yeah, yeah. Right. The back end.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Oh, backside packaging. Okay, I see. Well, for the backside packaging we're engaging with the customer in Taiwan and also engaging with customer in the US, right? We announced we have received the first tool development order from one of the U.S. advanced packaging houses. Definitely we have Ultra SAPS, this wafer tool for the advanced packaging. We're having engaged with multiple customer in Taiwan. Meanwhile, we just announced our panel low pressure cleaning for large and also announced this horizontal plating for the panel. These are two new product we're definitely address. The new trend also needs of this packaging requirement.
We're engaging with multiple customer right now and both you know in Mainland China and also in Taiwan also in the U.S,. We believe that will bring another exciting market for our new panel product. Plus, we're still engaging also developer additional new type, other type of the panel product too. We believe that will bring another our revenue growth potential, right? In this product portfolio.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay. Sounds like great progress all around. Thanks, David. Thanks, guys.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thank you, Suji.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. One moment for the next question. Our next question comes from the line of Charles Shi from Needham & Company. Please go ahead.
Charles Shi
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Needham and Company
Hi. A couple of questions. The first one looks like you're implying a half-over-half, largely flat for H2 of the year, but the shipment is probably higher in the H2. Just wanna also wanna clarify, when you say a shipment in the H2 of the year to grow, hopefully that's a half of a half comment or that's a sequential quarter-over-quarter comment? That's the first question.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
It's a half over half. Yeah. We'd expect shipments to be higher in the H2 than they were in the H1.
Charles Shi
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Needham and Company
Yeah. Any thoughts on the implied revenue guide for H2 being largely flat versus in the H1, and how should the people think about this?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Actually, revenue also H2 is higher than H1, right? You look at our middle point of the new segments.
Charles Shi
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Needham and Company
Okay. The second question is about the capital allocation. Definitely, the ACM Shanghai is already paying a dividend to ACM USA. I wonder, any thoughts on starting a dividend policy with the ACM Research investors, and especially when the ACM Shanghai probably going to see the lockup expiry pretty soon.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Okay, good point. We do have a dividend, right? Last year, and probably will continue this dividend, distributing to all the investors of ACM Shanghai, for near future. You talk about the lock-up of the ACM USA, for their share in China, Shanghai. I think in this moment our still major business from Shanghai and the ACM USA definitely can sell their share. However you can see that our status right now, we're keeping our share, right? The reason is that we do have a dividend and also ACM USA have a, the cash going on, and there's no reason to sell our precious share inside of China.
Charles Shi
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Needham and Company
Sorry, David, just wanna clarify. When I say dividend, I mean the dividend for ACM USA shareholders, not the ACM Shanghai shareholders.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. The dividend we got from ACM Shanghai and will come to ACM USA. This money, I think, will be reinvest into our market itself and also potential supporting in the R&D and for all the purpose, right? At this moment, we believe the cash we got from dividend, the best interest for the investor USA is reinvest back to the business instead of just distribute dividend to the ACM USA investor. We think that will be our major purpose for the dividends usage. Hey, Mark, anything you wanna add on that?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah. I mean, Charlie, Charles, I think it's an interesting question, but you know, echoing what David says, we don't have any plans to pay a dividend from the US. Yeah.
Charles Shi
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Needham and Company
Thank you.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. One moment for the next question. Our next question comes from the line of Mark Miller from The Benchmark Company. Please go ahead.
Mark Miller
Senior Equity Research Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Let me say congratulations, another very good quarter. Again, you're probably the greatest growth stock that at least in my universe, and hopefully the investors will respond to that more aggressively in the future. In terms of your evals going on, especially outside of China, can you give a little more color in terms of evals, in terms of what type tools and what countries?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay, sure, Mark. Definitely at this moment, and we do have our Canadian tool, right? As we go to a U.S. customer, we do have 2 type of tools. One is our SAPS, cleaning, and another one is really the backside, and also bevel clean, right? In the same customer. Recently, we're receiving another order from quarter developer from the U.S. advanced packaging house. We do have another evaluation tool or a PO tool from their European customer in the evaluation. Meanwhile, we're heavily engaged with a Korean customer for copper plating, right? And tool. That's in a demo status. You know, hopefully quickly we can ship to their production and for their final production evaluation.
We're talking with a few customers in Singapore and also in the U.S., and talk about our new cleaning capability, including TEBO and Tahoe and also our supercritical CO2 as really we designed for advanced technology evaluation, especially for 3D clean and also for acidic clean. That kind of, also, a powerful cleaning tool. We're engaging with multiple customers right now.
Mark Miller
Senior Equity Research Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Okay. In terms of your margin guidance, margins have been certainly above the target range regarding the margins being at the top of the guidance range. I assume that implies that your backlog, the margins of the tools in the backlog, are at or above your target range.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Mark, you wanna answer that?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
That's right, Mark. I mean we mentioned that for the year, our gross margins would be above the normal 40 to 45% range, really because they were stronger above the range for the H1 of the year. The rest of the year, we're expecting them to be at the upper end of our range. Yeah, I mean, our visibility on the margin profile for the end of the year is pretty good.
Mark Miller
Senior Equity Research Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. Once again, to ask question, please press star one one and wait for your name to be announced. One moment for the next questions. Next question comes from the line of Robert McKay from Blue Lotus. Please go ahead.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Hey there. Thanks for taking my question. Am I coming in clearly?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yes. Robert, please.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Oh, great. Okay, great. I did have a bit of a touchy question and, but I know, I think it might be important. I was wondering if we've evaluated if there's any there's been some discussion regarding some further restrictions on Chinese companies. I was wondering if there might be if we've evaluated what kind of impact there might be if that unfortunately does come through and what our thoughts are on that, and if there's anything we can talk about in that respect.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
You talk about this new rule for the export control? Is that what you mean?
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Yes, exactly.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. Well, I mean, again, right, we just heard some real market rumor. We're carefully I should say watch how the new rule come out, and ACM definitely will follow the law, right? U.S. law and follow Chinese law with the international business. You know, we're carefully. I mean, this moment, no speculation, but I will say that if something come out, it's not only ACM, right? A lot of U.S. companies got impacted too. We just want to watch out what's going on do whatever adjustment based on the new regulations come out.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Maybe the only thing that I would add to that is we take a deep step back and we look at the China WFE. You know, I think David's view, our view on WFE in China is that you know, pretty stable for this year, and you know, for the years to come that you know, the country will continue to invest in their production capacity. You know, we'll, like David mentioned, monitor any of the new regulations, of course. We'll follow the rules. You know, we generally anticipate WFE in China to remain pretty stable.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Got it. Thanks. Thanks for the clarity. In terms of our supply chain then, is there any potential impact to supply chain if any of these rumors do come to fruition?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
The supply chain at this moment, I see they're pretty stable right now, right? Obviously, we're looking for all different kind of supply chain and for mature product, we still buy U.S. components and but for the most nodes we are using non-U.S. parts. At this moment, we're also looking for multiple supply chain, those you know in the other country, also inside of China. We also qualify the local player of the components. We definitely have a plan to secure our supply chain and when any you know a new regulation come out and we can you know quickly switch into other alternative choice of the supply chain.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Okay. Got it. That makes a lot of sense. You have some backups. That's very good to hear. I had one more question I think is related to the private offering that we announced in January. I think we were going to do some private offering with our Shanghai shares. I was just wondering if we have any update in regards to that private offering, if there's any progress on that front and when we can-
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yes.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
expect to hear more about it. Yeah.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yes. Actually we're in the process to the final formal application, right? We know that the approval process for the secondary offering in China will take time. We estimate probably 6 to 8 months, even longer. Our approval probably we're expecting middle of next year, we might get it. Within another 1 year of the approval we got, we can probably receive the secondary offering based on market situation. Now, obviously we expect in that time we get our PECVD and the track system and also furnace, including our panel packaging tool, get in the market. We're choosing the right time and the right pricing to raise our second amount.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Okay. That makes a lot of sense. Thanks. I had one more question. It was just about if we have any new products that we can look forward to in the H2 of this year or in early 2025 that we can think about, or should we just wait until the announcement?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Well, obviously, we announced already, right? I mean, this Q2, we announced two products already. I wanna say we'll continue exploring a new product and obviously like this panel, right, we announced two. We're still working on the additional other type of the panel product and for this year, and probably we're gonna announce another new product when we get ready. Meanwhile, I still say we're still major focused on our Ultra C, what we're doing right now cleaning, copper plating, furnace, especially the furnace ALD and track and the PECVD. Our new product probably still along this major technology and also the product. We're not going to develop other new, which is completely new, more than this category I mentioned.
Robert McKay
Senior Research Associate, Blue Lotus Research Institute
Got it. That's very clear. Thank you very much. Also great results. Sorry for the touchy questions, but thank you very much. Yeah.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thank you, Robert.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. Once again, to ask a question, press star one now. There are no questions at this time. I would like to turn the call to management for closing remarks.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. Thank you, operator, and thank you all for participating on today's call and for your support. Before we close, Steven is going to mention our upcoming investor relations events. Steven, please.
Steven Pelayo
Managing Director, The Blueshirt Group
Thanks, David. Before we conclude, I just wanna give everyone a quick reminder on our upcoming investor conferences. On August 27, we will present at Jefferies Semiconductor, IT, Hardware and Communications Technology Summit at the Four Seasons Hotel in Chicago, in the United States. On September 4, we will present at Benchmark 2024 TMT Conference in New York City. Attendance at the conference is by invitation only. For interested investors, please contact your representative, sales representatives to register and schedule one-on-one meetings with the management team. This concludes our call, and you may now disconnect. Bye-bye.

content.text:
Steven Pelayo
Managing Director, The Blueshirt Group
Judgment for the future. However, they are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Those risks are described under risk factors and elsewhere in ACM's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Please do not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which reflect ACM's opinions only as of the date of this call. ACM is not obliged to update you on any revisions to these forward-looking statements. Certain of the financial results that we provide on the call will be on a non-GAAP basis, which excludes stock-based compensation and an unrealized gain and loss on short-term investments. For our GAAP results and reconciliations between GAAP and non-GAAP amounts, you should refer to our earnings release, which is posted on the IR section of our website and also on slides 13 and 14.
With that, let me now turn the call over to David Wang, who will begin with slide three. David?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thanks, Steven. Hello, everyone, and welcome to ACM Research Q4 and fiscal year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Please turn to slide three. I'm pleased with our Q4 results, which conclude a strong year. For Q4 2023, we delivered $170 million in revenue, up 57%. For the year, we delivered $558 million in revenue, up 43%. Profitability was good for both Q4 and the full year, with operating margin of 21% and 22% respectively. We ended the year with just over $300 million of cash and time deposits. For shipments, the shipments for Q4 were $140 million, down 29% year to year. Shipments for the full year were $597 million, up 11%.
On our Q3 call, we know the delay of shipment to several customers due in part to adjustment in their fab build outs. While we don't normally share our expectation for shipments, I will provide more color in this case. We view the low shipments for the Q4 to be a one-quarter event. We expect to deliver nearly all of the delayed tools during 2024. We expect the Q1 shipment to be much higher than the Q4 levels, even with the normal Chinese New Year shutdown. We expect the total shipment to grow faster than revenue for the full year 2024. Now I will discuss the key growth drivers both for the market and specific to the ACM. According to a third-party estimate, the overall mainland China WFE market grow around 15%.
If we exclude lithography tool, which more than doubled in China in 2023, we believe the rest of the market growth for China WFE was close to 5%. In any case, we attribute ACM higher growth rate of 43% to, one, a leading product portfolio for the China market, including auto bench clean and our ECP tool for the front-end and packaging. Two, continued spending and market share gain at our current customer. Three, broader participation with new customer in China. And four, good execution by our production and the service team. I will now provide detail on product. Please turn to slide four. Revenue from single wafer cleaning, Tahoe and supercritical cleaning product grew 48% in 2023 and represent 72% of total revenue. ACM offers what we believe in the industry the most comprehensive cleaning portfolio.
We support nearly 90% of all cleaning process fab for memory and logic devices. This coverage positions us as a key partner for both China mature nodes development and international markets. At the high end, we believe our flagship SAPS, Tahoe, and Tebow single-wafer cleaning products deliver technical feature not available from any of our competition. We entered into the 300mm auto bench cleaning market several years ago, is proving to be a significant winner for the mature node spending. We have delivered momre than 70 auto bench tools to date and note a very strong contribution in 2023 with good profitability. By our estimate, ACM become the largest China-based supplier for auto bench in 2023. For Tahoe, we made a good progress during the year. Our engineering team modified technical feature to meet production requirements for the key customer.
I'm pleased to report ACM has been qualified for mass production at several customers, and we expect a strong ramp with good orders for delivery in H1 2024. This is good for our customer and good for the environment as our proprietary Ultra C Tahoe design significantly reduce the consumption of the sulfuric acid. We continue to innovate in our cleaning and look forward to additional market share gain in 2024. We ramp up several key new product, including a barrel etcher cleaning tool, high-temperature SPM single-wafer cleaning tool, and the supercritical CO2 dry cleaning tool. Revenue from ECP, furnace, and other technology grow 33% in 2023 and representing 19% of total revenue. We hit an important milestone for this category in 2023 with more than $100 million in revenue. ECP demonstrated strong performance.
I want to note that our first tool shipment grew even higher than 33%. We are taking a good share of overall plating with a particularly strong growth in front-end processes in 2023. For furnace, 2023 was a customer development year with many evaluations on the way. We expect an even broader customer footprint and good revenue contribution in 2024. We also made great progress with our furnace ALD product development. In summary, we expect another year of strong growth in this product category in 2024. Revenue for advanced packaging, which excludes ECP but includes service and spare, grew 31.5% in 2023 and represented 9% of total revenue. This category includes a range of packaging tools, including coater, developer, scrubber, PR stripper, and wet etchers, and service and spare parts.
Last year, we also introduced Ultra C v vacuum cleaning tools, and we continue to explore new products and technology to participate in the next generation of advanced packaging. We believe ACM is the only company in the world that offers a full set of wet tool, polishing, and plating for advanced packaging. We expect advanced packaging to become more important as the industry looks for packaging innovation such as 2.5D and 3D in a photo and fan-out. These are critical for high performance computing applications such as AI, which is seeing increasing demand globally. Finishing up on product, we made good progress with our new track and PECVD platform. We are engaged in active dialogue with our key customer and intend to release additional evaluation tools this year.
As with our cleaning, plating, and furnace product line, our Track and PECVD platform boast the proprietary technology that position them as a successful choice for major customer globally, including both in and outside China. We are making a good progress in the evaluation of our Track tool. We are confident that the proprietary architecture of our Track tool is well suited for the high throughput required in next generation of distributed tools. We are engaged with multiple customers for our PECVD tool. We're expecting significant progress for PECVD product development and evaluation in 2024. Turn to slide five for our product suite. We estimate our product portfolio address a $16 billion market opportunity. Our business is now primarily driven by three major product groups: cleaning, plating, and advanced packaging.
We anticipate continued growth in this category and look to incremental revenue contribution from our newer products, starting with the furnace in 2024, followed by track and PECVD in 2025. Please turn to slide six. We remain committed to our medium-term $1 billion revenue target. We believe we can achieve this with a range of market share by product in the mainland China alone. We have achieved scale with a differentiated product that have been proven in China market, and we have put resource in place to address international markets. To be clear, long term, we see additional $1 billion plus opportunity from international markets. Moving on to the customer. Please turn to slide seven. In China, we are market leader in cleaning and plating tool, with sales to nearly every semiconductor manufacturers.
Our sales and service team are now driving deeper adoption of our products across this, customer base. Beyond established player, market growth is being driven by a influx of well-funded new entrants. For 2023, we had three 10% customers. SMIC was our top customer at 18% of sales. SiEn was our second-largest at 15%, and CXMT was our third at 13%. We had a stronger contribution from second- and third-tier semiconductor manufacturers, including power, analog, CMOS, image sensor, and compound semiconductors and other devices, and some new customers. Total 2nd and 3rd-tier players represent about 30% of our 2023 sales. On the international front, I'm pleased to report that a large US manufacturer qualified our first SAPS cleaning tool for revenue in Q1.
We also plan to deliver the Ultra C v backside cleaning and a bevel edge tool to this customer in Q2 2024. This demonstrates a deepening relationships which we believe can lead to production orders. Furthermore, this enhances ACM brand and position us to attract the new opportunities with other major global customers. Beyond the US, we saw our first evaluation tool, Ultra C SAPS five cleaning tool at a major Europe-based global semiconductor manufacturer in Q4. To support growth, we made progress on our facility expansion in China and other regions. Please turn to slide eight. In China, construction of our Lingang production and R&D center is nearly complete. We expect initial production in mid-2024. In Korea, we are making progress with a key customer.
As noted in the prior call, we have increased our commitment to support our objectives to address global market. We now have more than 150 employees in Korea with the facility, including sales, administration, small scale production, and the development lab with a clean room to support the internal R&D and wafer demos for the customer evaluation. We are making initial plans to build a new factory on the land we purchased early last year. We believe a strong commitment to Korea. We're improving our relationship with our key Korean customer. Our resources in Korea are providing another basis to support international customers in the US, Europe, and other part of Asia. In the US, we leased a facility in Oregon last year to add to our service support and demonstration capability for R&D and customer activity in the US and Europe.
I will now provide our outlook for the full year 2024. Please turn to slide nine. In early January, we introduced our 2024 revenue outlook in a range of $650 to 725 million. This, implying 23% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. We are reiterating this outlook today. We believe the China equipment market will grow in 2024. We expect our full year revenue growth for 2024 to outpace both China growth and global growth rates. Now let me turn the call over to our CFO, Mark, who will review details of our Q4 and full year results. Mark, please.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thank you, David. Good day, everyone. Please turn to slide 11. Unless I note otherwise, I will refer to non-GAAP financial measures, which exclude stock-based compensation, unrealized gain/loss on short-term investments. The reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to comparable GAAP measures is included in our earnings release. Also, unless otherwise noted, the following figures refer to Q4 2023. Comparisons are with Q4 2022. I'll now provide financial highlights for Q4 and full year 2023. Revenue was $170.3 million for Q4, up 56.9%. Revenue for single wafer cleaning, Tahoe and semi-critical cleaning was $122.3 million, up 63.9%. For the full year 2023, this category grew by 48.0%.
Revenue for ECP furnace and other technologies was $32.1 million, up 59.0%. For the full year 2023, this category grew by 33.4%. Revenue for advanced packaging, excluding ECP, services, and spares was $15.9 million, up 15.8%. The full year 2023, this category grew by 31.5%. Full year 2023 revenue was $557.7 million, up 43.4%. Total shipments were $140 million for Q4, down 29%. For the full year 2023, shipments were $597 million, up 11%. Gross margin was 46.8% for Q4 versus 49.7%.
For the full year of 2023, gross margin was 49.8% versus 47.4% in 2022. This exceeded our normal expected range of 40% to 45%. We do expect gross margin to vary from period to period due to a variety of factors such as sales volume, product mix, currency impacts. Operating expenses were $43.6 million for Q4, up from $34.8 million. R&D was $28.8 million versus $17.0 million as we invest in our new product initiatives. Sales and marketing was $7.2 million versus $11.8 million. The decline in sales and marketing was primarily due to a significant reduction of costs related to promotional tools. G&A was $7.6 million versus $6 million.
For the full year 2023, operating expenses were $154.4 million, up from $117.4 million. R&D was 15.1% of sales. Sales and marketing was 7.4% of sales, and G&A was 5.2% of sales, all for 2023. For 2024, we are planning for R&D in the 16% range, sales and marketing in the 7% to 8% range, and G&A in the 5.5% range. Operating income was $36.0 million for Q4, up from $19.2 million. Operating margin was 21.2%, up from 17.7%. For the full year of 2023, operating margin was 22.1% versus 17.2% in 2022.
For the Q4, we recorded a realized gain of $0.5 million from the sale of short-term investments. Recall that realized gains are included in the non-GAAP earnings. Income tax expense for the Q4 was $8.1 million versus $2.7 million. For the full year of 2023, income tax was $19.4 million versus $16.8 million in 2022. Net income attributable to ACM Research was $28.7 million for the Q4, up from $12.6 million. For the full year of 2023, net income attributable to ACM Research was $107.4 million versus $54.8 million in 2022. Net income per diluted share was $0.43 in the Q4, up from $0.19.
For the full year of 2023, net income per diluted share was $1.63 versus $0.83. I will now review selected balance sheet items. Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and time deposits $304.5 million at year-end versus $326.5 million at the end of the Q3. Total inventory at year-end was $545.4 million versus $507.4 million at the end of the Q3. The mix was split between raw materials, $235.1 million, work in process, $81.4 million, and finished goods inventory, $228.9 million. Inventory also included finished goods at our own facilities.
As David said, nearly all of the finished goods at our own facilities is expected to ship during the year 2024. Capital expenditures were $15 million in Q4 and $61.9 million for the full year. For 2024, we expect to spend about $80 million in capital expenditures. This will be primarily to complete our investment in Lingang and will also include remodeling the new headquarters for ACM Shanghai and investments in Korea and the US. That concludes our prepared remarks. Now let's open the call for any questions that you may have. Operator, please go ahead.
Operator
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask your question, you'll need to "press star one one" on your telephone. To withdraw your question, please "press star one one" again. Please wait for your name to be announced. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A roster. One moment for our first question, please. Our first question comes from the line of Suji Desilva with Roth MKM. Your line is now open.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Yeah. Hi, David. Hi, Mark. Congratulations on the progress. Great job there. Can you talk about the international customer? Sounds like you're making progress there. Just trying to gauge the pace of that. As you guided 2024 full year, do you have some contribution from international customer in that assumption, or would that be upside, and is it potential H1 timing, or is it most likely back-end loaded H2?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay. Thanks, Suji. I think this tool, we ship a year ago, right? Then through our service process engineer hard working, and then we have our first tool get their acceptance. This will be getting into the production, you know, their mass production. I want to say that this specific SAPS megasonic tool will address the customer needs, and we can see, you know, get a good cleaning performance and also much less particle consumption. That's really, you know, customer like the tool. We believe this definitely, you know, first tool qualification will lead to their additional order, you know, for the same customer. Right. Meanwhile, and as mentioned, we also have a second different tool, which is the backside and also bevel clean.
It was ordered by the same customer, and we ship them in Q2 of this year. Obviously that is just a key customer, you know, in the US, and we want this to be another example and also encouraging other big players to adopt our differential technology. Right. We'll say that will be the good outcome. Also, there's, of course, international, I call it, revenue contribution to our 2024 forecast. You know, we can see that too.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah, Suji, yeah. I just add for 2024, I mean, a lot of things go into our forecast. You know, 2024 will be a building year for us for the international, and we'd expect some additional contribution. You know, whether we get an order that ships or for one or several tools that ships this year or next year will depend on how big it can be for us.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. The second question is, can you just explain again the shipments and what the delays, what the dynamic was there? I maybe didn't catch that in the prepared remarks.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. I think in the Q3, we also mention about that, the delay. There it's because of our customer. They're building a plan, and there are certain, you know, I call it. I call the plan delay or the installation not enough, either resource or, you know, floor plan not fast enough. Anyway, there's continuing investment going on. Those portion of the delay, as I said, will be definitely delivered in 2024. You know, that's also added to our shipment. You know, those two has been built already. It's going to also, you know, save the cash. We spent a lot last year already. We'll see that happen.
I would say that also the total shipment, we expecting 2024, and there will be, you know, quite an increase, will be even more increased rate higher than the quarter revenue increase, right, in compared to 2023. This is another, I can say, a great year for us in 2024.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. That sounds like good momentum. My last question is around the overall demand environment. I'm trying to understand in China whether the memory market has stabilized and capacity is increasing again across NAND and DRAM, and maybe is someone like CXMT actually progressing to DRAM production versus development effort?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. I mean, you can see that, CXMT is still also the customer, you know, year 2023, right? We're expecting, you know, this memory business to continue to grow. Again, you know, it's all the, you know, memory in China is still multi-year expansion. We see that as good market, you know, for us, and also we see that continue to grow.
Suji Desilva
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
All right. Thanks, guys. Congrats again.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah. Thanks, Suji.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thank you.
Operator
One moment for our next question, please. Our next question comes from the line of Charlie Chan with Morgan Stanley. Your line is now open.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Thanks for taking my questions. David, Mark, happy Chinese New Year and Gong Xi Fa Cai, and congrats for a very solid 2023 results. My first question is actually on the full year guidance. Because I had the impression that your ACM Shanghai entity, they have a preliminary 2024 outlook, revenue to grow more than 30%. I remember you was like 37% YoY growth. I calculate your midpoint suggesting the ACMR is growing, like, 23% YoY. What was the discrepancy between your ACM Shanghai entity versus the parent company?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Well, you know, there's a slight difference like a revenue recognition rule, and we're using Chinese GAAP versus US GAAP. That's the primary reason show the difference of both. I got a forecast. In general, that is US GAAP will be first tool take a long time evaluation, and after that you can recognize, you know, repeat order just on the shipment, right? In China, GAAP is you have to, no matter it's new or it's a repeat order, you have to really install and basically accept, you know, kind of initial acceptance by the customer, then you can recognize revenue.
That slight difference shows the revenue difference. In other words, probably you can say China is a forecast, meaning that we have a lot of you know probably new tool and the new customer, right? That will quickly be recognized revenue versus the US recognition rule. That's the difference we see there.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
I see. Thanks, David. My next question is about the China CapEx sustainability, right? I mean, right now, as you said, right, it's for local sufficiency, but you also see that some of your major customer their gross margin already dropped to, like, 10%, gross margin, right? I'm a little bit worried about the sustainability. Any kind of signs or leading indicator we should you know, pay attention to, right? To check the China CapEx sustainability.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Well, I should say that, as we said, you know, a couple times before, is that China's fab is still in the multi expansion, no matter it's the logic or memory, right? Also, you know, a lot of, I call it mature nodes, is very related to the EV, IGBT, is still, you know, is still in the product, in the fab, in the building process. Also I wanna say another thing is the consumption of the chip, especially mature nodes in China is way higher than capability can be produced in China, right? You look at that gap, I'm still saying next few year in China and fab, this market will continue to grow.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Gotcha. Yeah, one last question, I will bring it back to the queue. A question to Mark. Since you are ramping up the Lingang new campus, can you give us some updated gross margin and also OPEX assumption for 2024?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah. Hey, Charlie. No, thanks for asking. I said in my prepared remarks, I gave some detail there, but I'll go ahead and repeat it. You know, we're anticipating our target model for gross margin is unchanged at 40% to 45%. Obviously we've done better than that for the last several years. That's gonna be the margin level that you know that's our target level. For the OPEX levels, and these are non-GAAP numbers, we expect R&D continue to invest pretty strong in R&D and, you know, you should always expect, you know, as we're a growing company, to spend at about a 16% level is our outlook for non-GAAP in 2024. Sales and marketing, you know, we expect in the 7% to 8% range, and then G&A about 5.5%.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Yeah, thanks for the recap. Those are guidance.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
You bet.
Operator
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, you'll need to "press star one one" on your telephone. One moment for our next question. Our next question comes from the line of Mark Miller with The Benchmark Company. Your line is now open.
Mark Miller
Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Well, first of all, congratulations, another great quarter. I just wanted to get a little more into the OpEx in the Q4. You did mention the S&M, sales and marketing was down. You said it was because of demo systems. I'm confused why that fell so much.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
It was a significant decline in the sales and marketing promotion tools. So we took that out of the sales and marketing expense. You know, going forward, you won't see that expense level in the sales and marketing. Yeah. We look at it kind of for the full year, sales and marketing was about 7.4% on a non-GAAP basis. We expect that sales and marketing level to be kind of in the 7% to 8%, in non-GAAP next year.
Mark Miller
Analyst, The Benchmark Company
You say you had a lot of quals underway. Can you give us a little more color on what's going on with your quals and timing of quals and in terms of when you expect revenue generation?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Oh, in terms of, yeah, David, he's asking about our evals at our customers. Maybe I'll let you address that for, and then I can add to it. But,
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
In general, right?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
I think, Mark, you know, our finished goods inventory, you know, is largely comprised of evaluation tools at our customers. Yeah, David.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Let me see, that is obviously there's just a finished goods in the customer side for evaluation, mostly the first tool. Those first tool can be either first tool for new customer, right? Especially if they're first time buyers, they wanna make sure those tool and not just qualify for tool itself, sometimes they qualify the whole production line to look at the yield to come out. That takes some time, right? Also, there's also the first tool is a pretty new, brand new tool, and then we need a customer to really evaluate that. We call it a beta tool, right? You need to really evaluate that, and that sometimes take a process, you know, one year, even a year and a half.
You know, it depends on how that tool, you know, first one to be mature, how mature it is. Those kind of tool will be considered as our, you know, first tool.
Mark Miller
Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Okay. Just final question. You previously said you were doing more investment in Korea to, I guess, get more business from SK hynix. Can you give us an update on what's going on there?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay, great. SK hynix actually is a real, long-term customer, right? We are fully engaged with the customer, I mean, SK hynix right now, because we're really emphasizing our investment, also expansion, our R&D force in, also manufacturing in Korea. We do have, you know, about 550 employees in Korea right now. As I mentioned, we bought the land and it will build through also through building factory there, at a, you know, future proper time. Key point I'm trying to say that is, we have multiple tools, like cleaning, copper plating, and including furnace, and then also a developmental PECVD and also track.
All these five tools we're trying to engage with the customer in SK hynix, and because of a relationship and also because of our local R&D force, and also we offer the customer with differentiated product and differentiated technology, which is quite a you know interest from the customer in Korea.
Mark Miller
Analyst, The Benchmark Company
Thank you.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thanks, Mark.
Operator
Thank you.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thanks.
Operator
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, you'll need to "press star one one". Please wait for your name to be announced. One moment for our next question, please. Our next question comes from the line of Christian Schwab with Craig-Hallum Capital Group. Your line is now open.
Christian Schwab
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Hey, guys. Fantastic year and great quarter. I'm trying to better understand, you know, the two or three reasons better, either from a product category standpoint or a customer standpoint, your conviction and your ability to outgrow WFE, not only in China, but also globally year over year.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay, great. I think you know the ACM there. We're start at beginning, you know, even from Bay Area, right? In ACM, our R&D philosophy is what I would call differentiation. Right? Each product we're building, like cleaning, you already know that SAPS, you know, TEBO and Tahoe is pretty our differential product. Same thing for the copper plating. Our goal is building differential product. In this moment, widely has been accepted by the local customer in China. With those differential product and the technology, I think we can penetrate or get into international, right? Example is we already get into the Panix, you know, and also we have one bigger manufacturer US adopted SAPS already. Also have a European company and also adopted SAPS make a strong cleaning tool.
Beyond that, as the next one is our Tahoe. Our TEBO plus we have a supercritical CO2 dry with Tahoe, with TEBO tool, but we will be excited for the pathway for cleaning too, right? Beyond that is also, as I said, we have, you know, furnace. For furnace ALD, including copper plating, and that was another very candid product, and to be able to penetrate international market. As I say, that is of course we're developing PECVD and the track also has our proprietary differential design point. ACM really developed their, you know, I call this the differential product, which really offers differentiation, offers the different benefit than our other competitor doing. That's our confidence and also our proven record. We can put a tool and sell in international market.
Christian Schwab
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Great. Congrats again on a very differentiated and better product than your competitors. Just as a quick last follow-up then is on the international front, you know, how much of the year-over-year growth are you looking for from that, I guess? I know it was kind of asked earlier, but you mentioned it numerous times as why you thought you would outgrow the market. I'm just wondering if you're willing to provide any clarity, more clarity there.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah. Hey, Christian, I'll hit that. In terms of our outlook, I mean, the range, we have a pretty small contribution from international this year. It's still gonna be, you know, kind of development. Really substantially, you know, most of that growth that we're planning for in 2024 is from the China market, the mainland China market. Yeah. New product cycles, customer, additional customer traction.
Christian Schwab
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Okay. I guess my very last question is, you know, the TAM for your products outside of China, you know, globally is substantially larger. You know, how many years do you think is reasonable for us to assume it takes for broad-based success internationally? It sounds like this year was a great building year. Initial shipments, you know, starting in 2024. Is that a, you know, 2026, 2027 or 2025 event or is it too early to tell?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Christian, this is a very good question. I think the way we're doing right now, obviously, it's quite a quicker fast growth in the mainland China market, right? As a lot of product we qualify here now. So those are, I think, our goal. We'll say, you know, reaching $1 billion even by China market only, right? We think in next few year we should be reach our goal. Simultaneously, you know, in the, you know, in a couple year, two years ago, we started also global market expectation. I mean, penetration. The key is really how we executing our international sales plan. Now we have, you know, hiring good people and a sales guy in the Korea, actually also in the US, in Europe.
We'll see that there quite a bit of progress. Let's put this way, you know, for the international market and as we talk to the customer, everybody's looking for backend again, you know, differentiation, right? With that in mind, and as I mentioned, core product we have right now, we do have confidence as the first, you know, I call the US customer adopt our tool. We see more of our customer may adopt additional or other tool too. We see that happen. Then you ask which year, how do we give you precisely. I think, as I said, we have bigger revenue with strong financial support from sales here, with also differentiated product, you know, definitely will penetrate, you know, into the international market.
If asking, you know, next few years is very exciting. You know, we have to, you know, quickly execute our plan and to quickly reach that goal. Eventually, as I mentioned a couple of times before, we are half from mainland China, half from outside mainland China, right? Like you said, the real revenue contribution actually much bigger outside mainland China.
Christian Schwab
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Thank you. That's great. No other questions. Thanks, guys.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thank you.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thanks, Christian. Yeah.
Operator
Our next question comes from Charlie Chan with Morgan Stanley. Your line is now open.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Thanks for taking my question again. I think the new customer contribution caught our eye, SiEn (Qingdao). It wasn't in our radar screen. I'm not sure why SiEn becomes such a big customer, and if you can provide some more details. Is that purely 12-inch equipment or also including some 8-inch equipment? Thank you.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. I think the primary we sell to the SiEn is a 12-inch tool, right? Their most expansion now is a mature node, so we actually sell a lot of our auto bench. They're probably the largest auto bench customer right now for us in China. Of course they also buy the full wafer, right? That's why primary driving that become the second largest customer in 2023. Looking forward, then also we're, you know, a very good relation and engage with them in the copper plating, furnace, and also on the line. That's another one we can say from the SiEn, right? They're a great customer, and we're happy with our, as I said, you know, our auto bench tool, the largely deployed in the SiEn's production line.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Yeah, it's a great business, right? I'm assuming you consult your lawyer about the U.S. export control before you ship in to all the customers, including SiEn, right? Is that the right assumption?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Well, I mean, we're strive to follow all the export control rules, right? As said here. For those- You know, restrict the customer, we have to be very carefully, you know, US parts, right? Personally involved and also, you know, non-US technology. Yeah. We're very carefully managing, controlling, and following them strictly with the standards, the US export control law.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Thanks, David. Next question is about the advanced memory, HBM. Can the company talk about your opportunity in Korea for the HBM production line? I think we asked that question last quarter as well. Also, there's some recent news about that China may also have their own HBM production. Can you comment about your potential opportunity in, you know, Korea and also China customers.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Well, let me put it this way. Obviously, you know, SK hynix, the number one provider, right? They're also technology leader, HBM. I think our current product definitely involve their process. Also we see the HBM either, you know, this is a copper plating tool, right? You know, TSV or the packaging, whatever they needed. That's the next tool we are working with, you know, closely with the SK hynix and their, you know, I should say rest of our other tool, you know, furnace, and we're working with them too. It's a lot of, including cleaning, by the way. Actually other cleaning other than we sold them, you know, SAPS megasonic, also working with their SK hynix too. It's a very good opportunity. AI, HBM, you know, is a greater, I call it demand and, greater driver.
Also they need a lot of differential technology, you know, further supporting in the HBM development in the future. In China, really not much we can hear right now, really, right? It's just, you know, I mean, not much we have right now. In other words, we're really focused on the outside China for HBM expansion for the business opportunity.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Yeah. Based on your comments and also other global equipment vendors, right? They talk about actually this year the global WFE revenue comes from the memory. Why SK hynix? Is that your kind of the top customer, or do you think this year SK hynix you know can contribute more than 10% of revenue given HBM opportunity and also the memory spending recovery?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Well, I mean, obviously more than, I mean other than SK hynix, also looking for other player, right? Is key here. The memory market, HBM, is really booming, right? That's key here. We see that. Demand there, as I mentioned, right? This is, for us, you know, cleaning, copper plating. It's really demand there. I don't know what time it comes back to 10%. Our customer is hard to predict right now. Really, and we'll see, right? Especially H2 or next year. It's really we wanna something recover from DRAM market.
Charlie Chan
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Gotcha. Thanks, David.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. One moment for our next question, please. Our next question comes from the line of Edison Lee with Jefferies. Your line is now open.
Edison Lee
Hong Kong Research, Industrials, Telecommunications, Thematic Research, Jefferies
Thank you. Thank you for taking my question. David and Mark, congratulations on a great quarter.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Okay.
Edison Lee
Hong Kong Research, Industrials, Telecommunications, Thematic Research, Jefferies
I have just one question, which is the contribution of your three customers for 2023, which has amounted to almost 50% of the revenue. Can you give us some color as to whether you think that those top three customers will continue to be top three customers in 2024? What is your expectation on the contribution of the top three customers in 2024?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. Actually, I looked at now this year's order, you know, list, right? The top three customer continue, I think, will grow, right? They're probably still our, you know, major customer. We see their, you know, additional fab or two, they have also their expansion plan. They are probably simultaneously building two fabs this year. They're building probably next year, you know, three fabs simultaneously, right? That's another bigger, I see their top, you know, customer will come back, you know, in our 2024 revenue contribution.
Edison Lee
Hong Kong Research, Industrials, Telecommunications, Thematic Research, Jefferies
Yeah. Maybe a related question is that based on your revenue guidance at this point that implies 20%+ growth, and so that's significantly below the growth rate in 2023. Do you think the key driver there is just some digestion period or is a matter of taking time for the evaluation tools to be recognized as revenue? What are the key factors for the slowdown in terms of the growth rate?
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah, I think the key driving force is I wanna say that China WFE market is continue. You know, people say maybe, I mean, slightly increase, at least a flat. I see that as number one important. But second most important is we have our gain for our, you know, I call it a higher growth rate is because we have a continue to have a new customer coming, and also we have a gain on market share from existing customer, and also do have a, like a furnace, what do the more contribution this year and for our revenue, right? So that's all added together. That's our, you know, give us a basis to forecast our growth rate higher than their, you know, their growth rate of the WFE market in China.
Edison Lee
Hong Kong Research, Industrials, Telecommunications, Thematic Research, Jefferies
Okay. Maybe the last one is that for 2024, what do you think is the percentage of overseas revenue in your guidance?
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yeah. Hey, Edison. We didn't break it out. But we did a couple other questions about that. We mentioned it wouldn't be a very significant contribution in 2024. You know, we expect that to build in the coming years, but it's not a very significant piece. We think it'll be bigger than it was this year. You got the numbers in. You'll get the international numbers shortly. It's not gonna become a huge, you know, I wouldn't expect it to be more than 10%. Right. Yeah.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Yeah. I should say growth rate is higher, right? I mean-
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Of course.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Obviously it's the number. The real absolute number, like you said, you know, we're still a fraction of the total revenue.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Yep.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
All right.
Edison Lee
Hong Kong Research, Industrials, Telecommunications, Thematic Research, Jefferies
Okay. Got it. Thank you very much.
Mark McKechnie
CFO and Treasurer, ACM Research
Thanks.
Operator
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to hand the conference back over to Steven Pelayo for closing remarks.
Steven Pelayo
Managing Director, The Blueshirt Group
Okay, great. Thanks, Mark, and David, and thank you all for participating on today's call. Before we conclude, I just wanna give everyone a quick reminder on our upcoming investor conferences. On 18 March, we will present at the 36th annual ROTH Conference in Dana Point, California. Attendance at the conference is by invitation only. For interested investors, please contact your respective sales representatives to register and schedule one-on-one meetings with the management team. This concludes the call, and you may now disconnect.
David Wang
CEO and President, ACM Research
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect. Everyone, have a wonderful day.
